dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Make `_first_merge_index` detect the production reconvergence merge (which is written `if ! git merge ...`) rather than only lines that literally start with `git merge ` (currently only the `git merge --abort` line matches for production).
evidence: reconcile-bridge.yml:338: `if ! git merge --no-edit origin/tickets 2>&1; then` — after .strip() begins with `if !`, not `git merge `
reconcile-bridge.yml:339: `git merge --abort 2>/dev/null || true` — the only production line whose strip begins with `git merge `
search_files for 'git merge' in reconcile-bridge.yml returned no matches for a line beginning with it (the retry merge is guarded by `if !`), confirming the real merge is not detected by the helper
dropped.finding: The lint test's `_first_merge_index` matches lines starting with `git merge `, but the production workflow's actual reconvergence merge is written as `if ! git merge --no-edit origin/tickets 2>&1; then` (strips to `if !...`, which does NOT match). The only production line that matches is `git merge --abort` (line 339). So for the production job the ordering assertion `production_config < _first_merge_index(production)` is anchored on the merge-ABORT line, not the real merge — a semantically incorrect and fragile anchor.
scenarios: A refactor that moves or renames the `git merge --abort` line without touching the real merge would make the production assertion match a different line or fail spuriously.
The test claims to prove 'driver configured before the reconvergence merge' but for production actually proves 'before the merge-abort line'.
dropped.suggested_fix: Match the merge substring anywhere in the command (e.g. `"git merge --no-edit" in line` or a regex on `git merge ` not preceded by nothing) instead of `line.startswith("git merge ")`, and exclude `git merge --abort`, so both workflows anchor on their real reconvergence merge.
